reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) states that slow kinetics lead to phase segregation and that the laser method overcomes immiscibility to produce uniform HENAs, supporting the first two premises. However, there is no evidence that the resulting structure retards high-temperature diffusion or that slower methods cause ordering during formation, nor that synthesis rate controls subsequent thermal stability—these are extrapolations beyond the cited data.
premises: Slow synthesis kinetics cause phase segregation in HENAs
Ultrafast laser reduction yields a kinetically trapped, uniformly mixed disordered structure
The disordered structure retards atomic diffusion at high temperatures
Slower reduction allows atomic mobility that initiates ordering/segregation during formation
Synthesis rate governs subsequent high-temperature structural stability
